requirement: One dated table of measured platform constraints, each with its evidence and workaround; nothing depends on a behaviour that is not a row.
kind: MECHANISM (purpose: stand only on measured behaviour)
note: No evidence against it (audit A). A record of measurements; listed in section 5.

requirement: Depend only on acts the committed approvals cover and that were measured to pass; archiving sessions and switching off or deleting tasks are housekeeping, never needed for correctness.
note: D9 names permission refusals first among the interruptions. The modifying note was written in by the coordinator as the owner's chat word (D10; see the provenance note after section 4).

requirement: Hard permission rules live in allow and deny lists, which run before the classifier; the classifier is never the policy.
note: Replaced in the Ledger by GAP-6 on 3 Nov; the deny-list half stands (F-PLAT-5). Measured 1 Nov: an allow rule does not take session and task acts out of the classifier.

requirement: No step runs longer than the in-session background limit of about thirty minutes; anything longer is a CI workflow.
note: Bears on the walks of D6(iii) and D7: the two late deploy-and-walk runs took 60 and 64 minutes (product_side §6, CI time).

requirement: No session starts its own successor; depth stays at most 3.
note: Platform fact: sessions are created only from depth 0 to 2. The modifying note was written in by the coordinator as the owner's chat word (D10; provenance note).

requirement: A scheduled task is never required for correctness; a wake is a convenience and the record is read at every wake regardless.
note: D2 and D4 ("slots are actively filled") lean the same way: ready work does not wait on a timer.

requirement: A session works on one repository, the product's; the process is a read-only clone at a pinned commit.
note: Platform fact behind it: a session reads the deny list only when it holds one repository. The cost of moving the pin is at MNT-5.

requirement: GitHub acts a session cannot take run on GitHub's runner, by workflows with the owner's tokens as secrets.
note: Under D1 the owner's part is a GitHub setting (the secrets).

requirement: Every credential is gathered once and checked at every tranche open; a missing grant stops a tranche from opening, never a step midway.
kind: PURPOSE (mechanism: a check at tranche open)
note: Conflict CHK: the tranche-open check is a blocking check that is not one of D6's three tests. The purpose (no step fails midway for a missing grant) stands either way. The evidence against a grant check concerns its every-job-start form only (F-SET-3).

requirement: A session's platform status is never read as its work state; the record is.
At most a handful of command hooks, each for a zero-exception rule, each with a legitimate blocked exit; none that hold a turn or judge text.
note: D9 leans the same way. Today there are none.

requirement: No model judge sits between a session's message and the owner.
Nothing holds a turn; when the owner says stop, the session stops in that turn.
note: The owner's own P19 note keeps this beside "never idles": the mechanism for urgency is "never anything that holds a turn".

requirement: No /goal and no model judging the transcript; a job that stops early is caught by status and the sweep.
note: D9 ("Claude stopping short of work it could do") bears on it: status and the sweep detect, they do not continue the work. Note recorded by the coordinator from the owner's "Yes, as recommended" (D10; provenance note).

requirement: Every gate or hard rule offers the model a legitimate exit, "blocked", recorded and visible to ARCH.
note: Used 165 times in the week; in 72 the job said the work was done and "job complete" refused (product_side §6d). That is evidence about the gates, not against the exit.

requirement: Keep the durable and transient split, but move coordination traffic to pull-request bodies, comments and issues, or to a separate bookkeeping repository.
note: Evidence against the home Process3 built (an orphan state branch): 12,881 commits, 70% of all commits from 3 to 9 Nov (product_side §3). The line itself names the alternatives; the definition must say which holds transient state.

requirement: One writer per file.
note: Held as a nudge (ledger_map).

requirement: One status command reads the whole state a role needs from git and prints it with sizes; a successor of any role starts from it alone.
kind: MECHANISM (purpose: any session can be replaced from the record)
note: Leans with D9 (no handoff scanning): a successor starts from status alone.

requirement: Record writes by the architecture session never cost a job a gate run or a completion.
note: Missed in Process3: 294 of 789 gate runs were started by record changes (product_side §4). That is evidence the purpose was not met, not evidence against it.

requirement: A remote act is recorded as done only from the tool call's result, never from its request.
An address is read from git at the moment of sending, and an address change is on the branch before it is announced.
note: Stands as long as addresses and messages remain.

requirement: The record of a halted build is complete: a fresh session's status tells everything open, idle, merged, unmerged and owed, with no transcript.

Keep a reading audit that judges reading by what a session can cite from the end of a document, and shrink documents so the question rarely arises; the start command prints the reading set with sizes.
note: Evidence: the audit was never built in nine days (ledger_map: REC-8 "no audit", Gap, later gate), and the one reading restraint that held was a byte cap (causal_forensics, headline). The reading rule itself is P20, kept. Also an audit outside D6's three (section 5).

requirement: The build ledger is a schema-constrained JSON file with one mutable field per entry, not free-form markdown.
note: Owner's note: "Try this, but measure the experience with an open mind as to whether it's work or not." Evidence: 105 of 508 landings changed nothing but process/ledger and process/metrics (product_side §2); the census built on the ledger was loosened after 7.3 hours (change_sample PR 204). The measure the Foundations set for it (corruption, bypass) is in no post-mortem file.

requirement: A CI check fails any commit that adds a file over a set size or under a transient path; a scheduled prune removes finished transients.
note: Evidence: 947 findings on its first run (5 min 23 s) and false-positive repairs in seven later merges (change_sample PR 1); 495 runs in eight and a half hours, 403 on branches where "nothing reads it" (change_sample removal 116). The purpose is P23, kept.

requirement: Decisions go to short decision records the moment they are made, each in its own file, never as a line in a long plan.
kind: MECHANISM (purpose: a decision has a visible home a requirement can cite)
note: D9 ("every user utterance being turned into a new rule until the rules overflow") bears on the mechanism. Evidence: DECISIONS.md went from nothing to 49 KB and 31 headings in four days, in one file (verify_numbers §7, §8). D10: a record is the owner's only if he wrote the words (23 of the 26 PD records are headed "coordinator").

requirement: Modules sit in one total order, each in one layer, lower first; uses are declared and matched by imports; a violation fails the gate.
note: D3 restates the order; D6(i) puts the uses-match-imports check inside each job's module tests. The clause "each in one layer" is ended by D5. Facts for the definition: the check was never in the tool's gate (ledger_map Gap), and the map today has three later-pointing uses and one cycle, so 27 of the 65 modules with work can never be ready under D5 until they are repaired (no_layers_width §2).

requirement: Each file has one owner module; a job writes only its module's paths and tests and the strike of its own marks.
note: Conflict CHK: the ownership check in the gate and the merge is a blocking check outside D6's three. The purpose stands (D3: "Each module is updated and tested by a single job"). No evidence against the check: one false refusal, repaired on 3 Nov (change_sample PR 46, cited by audit A).

requirement: A test asserts on a text's key, never on its words; every user-facing sentence lives once in the word table.
note: Owner's word of 30 Oct. A standard for how tests are written; its gate check was never built (ledger_map Gap). Section 5.

requirement: Architecture, ownership, format and coverage checks run only against the job's module in its gate, layer checks when a layer closes, and over the whole product before a release or on the owner's word.
note: D5: "The layer construct is dropped". D6: "No regression or deploy-and-walk between layers" and "The full regression is ended; the internal walk replaces it". The module-scope clause survives only as far as those checks count as part of test (i) (section 5). Evidence that the timing did not serve: no deployment for 80 hours while 308 landings went in, and the next walk found 1,691 failures (product_side, summary 3).

requirement: Every check and gate finding names module, file and line in one machine-readable result that status reads; a red is never searched for in a log.
note: Not fully delivered in Process3: "the gate rows carry no reason field" (product_side, "What could not be established").

requirement: Each module's requirements file has a public part and a private part, every statement under a permanent id.
kind: MECHANISM (purpose: users see what they may depend on; ids can be cited)
note: The public part is what defines a module's interface for D3.

requirement: A requirement states behaviour at the interface, never an implementation; an ambiguity is removed by rewriting the text.
A figure at a scale beyond the suite is a measurement with its own plan id, never a test line; a review never counts an untaken measurement as a gap.
note: By the line's own words a measurement, not a test; listed in section 5.

requirement: A not-yet-met mark is struck only by the job that meets it, in its own commit.
note: Evidence is against the heavier Process3 form only: a named test demanded for every struck mark was removed after 5.8 days (change_sample PR 40).

requirement: A change to what a provided service means goes to the owner only where it changes what the product does for its users and the canon is silent; every other change is ARCH's, recorded once.
note: D3 adds that every interface change notifies the users. Under D2 only the work that depends on the owner's answer waits.

requirement: A size cap on a module's requirements triggers a split or consolidation before any job starts, with the number measured on the real product; never a refusal at a job's start.
note: Evidence: the cap was built as a refusal of "job complete" at 70,000 bytes and was overridden 32 times of 32 with no catch; it drove 30 split requirement files, 64 commits and 47 block texts, and total requirement bytes did not change (product_side §6b, §6d). The purpose is P6, kept.

requirement: Only explicitly marked words of the owner's become decisions; a ruling lives only until the requirement it refines is rewritten to absorb it, then it is deleted.
note: D9 and D10 restate it.

requirement: Work is structured as layers within rounds within tranches; nothing else about a product's size or shape is assumed.
note: D5 ends the layer term: "The layer construct is dropped". Rounds and tranches stand and are redefined by D6(iii) and D7. The definition must state the structure that remains.

requirement: A plan is written from the work that remains; an entry is deferred only for one of three named reasons.
Work found while a round runs is placed at once: in the running job, else a later START, else the completion round.
note: The clause "a later layer's START" loses its layer (D5). The route earned its place: 183 found marks raised, 132 met (product_side §5).

requirement: The completion round has its own file, distinct from the next tranche's list.
note: Made moot or changed by D5 and D7: in Process3 the completion round was what followed the plan's last layer (DECISIONS.md PD-12); under D7 rounds repeat until one completes without failures. The definition must say whether a separate completion file remains.

requirement: Pause and resume are first class: the owner's word is recorded once in the plan's status line; every session reads it at its next status and takes no new step.
note: Evidence against the mechanism: "the 3 Nov halt switched tasks off by hand" (ledger_map, PLN-5), and process activity ran for 2 h 20 min after the 9 Nov stop (product_side §8). D1: stopping must not need a command or a hand-switched task from him.

requirement: A tranche's report states elapsed time, work finished, deferrals with reasons, work left, cost, and the share of cost that was process overhead.
note: D7 fixes when a tranche ends. Cost was often unobtainable (product_side, "What could not be established"); SES-9 says to name it unmeasured. A report; section 5.

requirement: Two products may run tranches at once on one account; nothing in the process names a product.
note: The owner restated it on 8 Nov (DECISIONS.md BD-R2). D4 does not say whether the 8 slots are per product or per account; the definition must.

source: Foundations: What this process is for
requirement: The process exists to meet the standards the owner sets in two roles, product manager and software engineer.

source: Foundations: What this process is for
requirement: The owner's audience attributes are carried in the canon and each module's requirements, cited by id.

source: Foundations: What this process is for
requirement: Lanes for design areas the owner identifies; the UX lane is always there.
kind: MECHANISM (purpose: the owner's UX and design standards have a keeper)
note: No decision ends lanes and there is no evidence against them (see SES-14).

source: Foundations: What this process is for
requirement: The owner's engineering standards are carried by the module order and layers, the checks, the gate, measurements at scale (REQ-3), and the cost metrics.
note: Three carriers are changed by decision or evidence: layers (D5), the checks and the gate (D6: three tests), and the cost metrics (JOB-10's evidence). The definition must name what carries scalability, performance and cost.

source: Foundations: What this process is for
requirement: Put correct, working product behaviour that meets its requirements onto main, quickly and cheaply, so that it survives (P1).

source: Foundations: What this process is for
requirement: Nothing else is output: a rule, record, check or test has value only as far as it serves that.
note: D9 restates it.

source: Foundations: The human and the AI
requirement: The owner defines the project; ARCH does everything else and decides everything technical and detailed (P17).
note: D1 and D8 restate it. What bounds ARCH's own changes to the process is the conflict at F-HUM-12.

source: Foundations: The human and the AI
requirement: ARCH keeps the record, manages the development environment, takes the owner's input and reports to him in plain words as done.

source: Foundations: The human and the AI
requirement: In the middle ground both offer opinions, options and recommendations; neither is dogmatic.
note: D11 is in the same spirit.

source: Foundations: The human and the AI
requirement: The owner's time is the scarcest resource; he sees rendered pages, with options and a recommendation, only for what is his.

source: Foundations: The human and the AI
requirement: An act only the owner can take is named and walked through in plain steps.
note: D1 narrows such acts to GitHub or Cloudflare permission and rule settings.

source: Foundations: The human and the AI
requirement: By default a job, layer or tranche merges on a green gate without the owner; a public release waits for him; he may ask for his approval before a particular merge.
note: Layer is ended by D5. The public-release clause is the conflict at GAP-7. His approval of a particular merge is a gate only at his own request (section 5).

source: Foundations: The human and the AI
requirement: The owner does not edit files or enter commands; the few steps the platform forces at onboarding are kept as few as possible.
note: D1 restates and tightens it: settings in GitHub or Cloudflare only, "very occasionally".

source: Foundations: The human and the AI
requirement: When ARCH is unsure whether a question is the owner's, it decides by this section and says how it read it.

source: Foundations: The human and the AI
requirement: When a mechanism cannot be built or a better one is measured, ARCH restates the line with its purpose unchanged and reports it in one line; only a change to what a line asks for comes to the owner (his word, 4 Nov).
note: D8 agrees: he is not a gate for changes of mechanism. This table uses the same split.

source: Foundations: The human and the AI
requirement: A tranche can run from open to close with no one watching: every stop is a named blocker, ARCH starts other work meanwhile, and only a blocker only the owner can clear reaches him (GAP-1).
note: D2 restates "can run" as how the process runs.

source: Foundations: The human and the AI
requirement: Caution is a cost, paid only against a measured failure or the owner's word; a reviewer's "what if" is one line in a report.
note: D9 restates it.

source: Foundations: The human and the AI
requirement: Every problem is an architecture bug: ARCH finds why, corrects the design by rewriting the line it belongs to, and builds the correction; a workaround for the moment is not a fix (owner's direction, 2 Nov; repeated 7 Nov).
note: Conflict AUTH: D8 ("when a flaw in the process is found it must be fixed") and D9 (no piling on of tests, reviews, gates and checks) pull against each other on this line, given the record: 46 of 121 check-adding merges (38%) answered a failure of the process's own earlier machinery, and 47% of sampled additions were removed or loosened after a median 28 hours (change_sample, summary and §2). Audit C's uncounted cross-reference X-1 is this same sentence.

source: Foundations: The human and the AI
requirement: The default answer to a finding with nothing measured behind it is no change; a rule, check, review round or measurement exists only against a measured failure or the owner's word (GAP-3).
note: D9 restates the purpose and D6 caps the tests. Evidence against the citation mechanism: its audit was never built and "every rise cited" (causal_forensics §7); 44% of sampled additions guarded something never observed (change_sample, summary).

source: Foundations: The human and the AI
requirement: When in doubt, run the product and let it show what matters.
note: D6(iii), the internal walk, is of this kind; the checks that held up were the ones that ran the product (change_sample §5).

source: Foundations: The human and the AI
requirement: A question that is the owner's becomes his decision, and a design, before anything is built on it (P21).
note: Under D2 only the work that depends on the answer waits.

source: Foundations: The human and the AI
requirement: Questions that are the owner's are asked in one place, numbered, with a column for his word; a decided question is never asked again.
note: D10: the column holds only words he wrote.

source: Foundations: The human and the AI
requirement: A word the owner gives in chat is written into the walk-through by ARCH.
note: D10: "only words the owner himself wrote count as his word", so a session's transcription cannot be what makes a word his. Evidence: of 218 attributions to him, 64 were his traceable words and 48 were a session's own decision written as his (bob_naming, table total; 47 of the 48 by the coordinator).

source: Foundations: The shape in one paragraph
requirement: Git and GitHub carry all state; messages only wake; each job's coordination is in its pull request.

source: Foundations: The shape in one paragraph
requirement: One architecture session per product plans from the build state and routes; job sessions each build one module as one draft pull request, every ready module of the open layer at once; in-session workers do bulk reading, review and sub-tasks.
note: Open layer is ended by D5, which gives the readiness rule; D4 gives the bound (8 job slots, actively filled); D10 renames the architecture session. "One module, one job" is D3.

source: Foundations: The shape in one paragraph
requirement: Nothing the model says is evidence: a job's claim is a receipt, the gate is CI, the revert check proves tests real, and branch protection is the last word.
note: The purpose stands. Two of its named mechanisms are in question: the receipt (JOB-7, removed on the owner's word on 9 Nov) and the revert check (JOB-12, conflict CHK).

source: Foundations: The shape in one paragraph
requirement: Rules are few, each cites a failure, and each names the tool that enforces it or is labelled a nudge.
note: D9 restates "few". Evidence against citation as the brake: every growth was cited (causal_forensics §7), and check-adding stayed at 41% of merges before and after the owner's 5 Nov instruction (change_sample, summary).

source: Foundations: The shape in one paragraph
requirement: The process is measured by its false-done rate and its cost per surviving pull request; these are the standing judge of every other line.
kind: MECHANISM (two metrics) for a PURPOSE (an honest judge)
note: Evidence: 218 of 220 jobs read COMPLETE and 98.8% of landed lines survived while 147 of 157 live walk steps failed (product_side, summary 2 and 3), so both metrics would have read healthy on a product that did not work. D7 makes a failure-free round the test of a tranche. The definition must say what judges, and the owner should see any change to his judge.

source: Foundations: The shape in one paragraph
requirement: The process is re-tested one component at a time at each model release.
note: A trial of the process, not of the product (section 5). Leans with D9.

requirement: Each property names what holds it; one held only by text is a nudge and is marked so; the record exposes a violated nudge at the next status.
note: Evidence about nudges as holders: restraint was a nudge read once while checks were code that refused on every call (causal_forensics, headline 3).

requirement: Done means merged; main never moves while a tranche runs.
A job's tests must fail when its change is reverted.
note: Conflict CHK: this property is held by the revert check (JOB-12).

requirement: Work is never lost or left waiting: no session ends a turn while work it can do remains, and everything is pushed before any turn ends.
note: D9 ("Claude stopping short of work it could do") and D4 ("slots are actively filled") restate the purpose. Evidence against the mechanisms built for it: the idle alarm misfired for 2 h 22 min and the idle check before every command cost 1,564 git processes (change_sample PRs 139, 140). The Foundations hold it as a nudge.

requirement: The process is pinned per tranche and changed only by a recorded act.
note: D8: the recorded act is not the owner's merge. The cost of frequent pin moves is at MNT-5.

requirement: The process and the product are separate; the process lives in its own repository (P2).
The product's build state lives at the paths the product's config names, is written only through the process, and is what tells ARCH what to do.
Sessions are kept short, because cost grows with context times turns; ARCH refreshes at a threshold.
note: How a refresh happens without handoff scanning (D9) is open at SES-2 and SES-3.

requirement: The handoff is a pointer set on one screen, written by the tool, never by hand.
note: D9 lists "handoff scanning" among the interruptions; the definition must say how a successor starts. The line as written was not what ran: 26 hand-written handoff notes became the rulebook (causal_forensics, headline 4 and §3).

requirement: No branch is deleted or force-pushed; the owner's approvals and rulesets forbid both.
note: Rulesets are the kind of setting D1 leaves to him.

requirement: A session acts only on what it has read in full or measured; every claim names its source; anything unread or unmeasured is unknown; a cause is named, and a fix written, only once evidence shows it (P20).
The owner decides only the layers and modules that carry product capability; the rest is ARCH's.
note: Layers is ended by D5. The product's layer contracts are placement rules, not scheduling (no_layers_width §5); D5 does not say whether they remain as text.

requirement: Each module's file states the services it provides, the services it uses by module, its invariants and the product requirements it satisfies; it may suggest but never require an implementation; it is concise because it is read whole (P5).
note: The provided-services part is what an interface change is measured against (D3).

requirement: A module fits in one reading: one session can read in full its code, its requirements and those of the services it uses (P6).
A change needing no judgment across many modules is one mechanical pass by a worker while no job runs, with one full test run in CI; where judgment is needed, the module gets its own job (P7).
note: D3: "Each module is updated and tested by a single job". D6: "The full regression is ended; the internal walk replaces it". The pass never had a procedure (ledger_map: P7 gap). The owner kept this clause on 3 Nov ("Keep the mechanical pass, shorter"), so he should see that D3 and D6 end it.

requirement: One rulebook per role, at most ten rules on one screen, rewritten in place and never appended; when the owner raises a problem a rule is rewritten and no ruling is added (TXT-3).
note: D9 restates the purpose. The ten-rule cap held all week (verify_numbers §7).

requirement: Each role's starting prompt names its own text in the pinned process, so a role loads only its rules (TXT-5).
The principles are trimmed so each role loads only the few that govern its stage (TXT-4).
note: On trial at the owner's word ("I'm skeptical, but let's try"); not measured. Section 5.

requirement: The product's CLAUDE.md is under thirty lines, written by ARCH line by line, and changes without the owner's approval (his word, 1 Nov).
kind: PURPOSE (the owner's word about his time)
note: D8 agrees. The approvals block inside the file is the conflict at GAP-6. Fact: the file ended at 22 lines and 8,664 bytes, all growth from 16 owner patches (product_side §6a).

requirement: Every line in any instruction file is failure-backed, non-inferable from the code, or tool-enforced; lines are deleted on review (TXT-2).
note: As TXT-2.

requirement: Every text names its audience and speaks plainly (TXT-7).
Each role's reading set is fixed and printed with sizes (SES-5).
note: A printed measure that blocks nothing (section 5).

requirement: Nothing is ever refused for size: budgets are fractions of the model's window in one table, never bytes in code; an overrun is measured and reported, never refused (SES-6).
note: As SES-6: a candidate for the process's own instruction texts only.

requirement: A summary is an option ARCH may take, never a requirement (SES-7).
A job is a draft pull request from job/<module> to the tranche branch; its body is its START, its report is a comment, its merge is its completion.
note: Fits D3 and D4 (a slot frees when the job "completes and is merged").

requirement: A START names only acts the tool supports, each as the command the job runs.
A module's earlier unmerged work is taken in by a tool command on the job's own branch.
kind: MECHANISM (purpose: no work lost, no hand-copied diffs)
note: The need is real now: 27 unmerged November job branches (product_side §1, §5).

requirement: A job is never restarted for a process reason; a blocking flaw holds it at its next command, the fix lands, and the same job continues.
note: The purpose stands and D8 agrees that the flaw is fixed. Evidence against the mechanism as it ran: 116 pin moves reaching the product a median 3 to 21 minutes after merging, 1,339 sync merges against 508 landings, and 3.1 job starts per job (product_side §4, §5).

requirement: A job's completion runs locally only checks that take seconds; the gate is CI. It pushes, posts its report, marks the pull request ready and sets COMPLETE.
note: The receipt part of the report is at JOB-7. The seconds-long local checks are in section 5.

requirement: An unmerged job whose session is gone is restartable by one command that keeps its branch and pull request.
A job's report carries Met, Evidence as a machine-readable receipt, and what it found elsewhere; a flaw in another module goes to ARCH as a report.
kind: MECHANISM (receipt) and PURPOSE (what a job finds elsewhere reaches ARCH)
note: The candidate is the receipt only. Evidence: no catch in 1,187 gate runs, about 20 follow-up merges, and the owner's "get rid of it completely" on 9 Nov (change_sample Case 3; DECISIONS.md PD-21). He decided it for Process3; he must confirm it for Process4. The found-elsewhere half stands (F-JOB-6).

requirement: A job never commits a generated artifact.
note: No check was built for it (ledger_map Gap).

requirement: A job ends a turn only COMPLETE or on a named wait with everything pushed.
note: D9 ("Claude stopping short of work it could do") restates the purpose; nothing enforces it but the rule and the record.

requirement: A job's reading set is recorded at its start and its tokens at its end, per attempt, so restarts are never counted as jobs.
note: Evidence: a required cost figure "blocked every job complete" and was removed 45 minutes later (change_sample PRs 105, 106); sessions "frequently could not obtain a cost figure" (product_side, "What could not be established").

requirement: Each job runs in its own checkout; its cost per attempt is an alarm the sweep reads, not a cap.
note: Replaced in the Ledger by GAP-2; disposition as GAP-2.

requirement: A revert check in CI: with the production change reverted, the job's new tests must fail.
kind: PURPOSE (tests are real; mechanism: a check in CI)
note: Conflict CHK: a check that is not one of D6's three, unless it counts as part of each job's own module tests. Evidence both ways: it is named in 61 block texts, and on 9 Nov real test repairs were dropped because it could not accept them (product_side §6c, §6d); a commit restoring it cites the owner's keep-or-drop answer of 6 Nov (change_sample PR 185), and the false-done count rests on it.

requirement: Mutation sampling on critical paths, nightly, after the first tranche, payment and data paths only.
note: D6: "exactly three tests and no others, ever". Never built (ledger_map).

requirement: One module or one feature per session; after two failed corrections, a fresh session whose brief says what was corrected and why.
note: The owner's own words.

requirement: The gate runs in CI, once per pull request tip, and never in a session.
note: The gate is where test (i) runs. Owner's word of 30 Oct.

requirement: The gate runs the module's own suite, its layer's tests if any, and the checks scoped to the module; it never runs another module's suite.
note: D6(i) restates it. The clause "its layer's tests if any" is ended by D5 and D6. The module-scoped checks other than uses-match-imports are in section 5. Evidence for "never another module's suite": users' suites in the provider's gate cost +7.6 minutes at the median, caught 0 of 20, and were reverted after 2.2 hours (change_sample PR 112).

requirement: A change to a provided service reaches its users through the architecture session's requirement notice and each user module's own job.
note: The purpose is D3 and D6(ii). Evidence against the mechanism as built: 178 notices became 2,707 notifications, 90% of 2,342 verdicts were "not affected", and 187 notice test files (9,321 lines) were written (product_side §6c, §6d). The purpose earned its place: 241 verdicts were "affected" (product_side §6d, §9.3).

requirement: A session acts only on what it has read in full or measured; every claim names its source; a cause is named only once evidence shows it.
note: Its audit is REC-8, a candidate.

requirement: A question that is the owner's (by P17 only) becomes his decision and a design before anything is built; a lane has one area of focus and delivers designs, reached through ARCH; lanes stay as SES-14 settled them.
note: Under D2 only the work that depends on the answer waits.

requirement: A release is cut from the open tranche, proven by the full regression, deployed and walked; what a walk finds becomes a round's entries; what it produces is kept only until analysed.
note: D6 ends "proven by the full regression" ("The full regression is ended; the internal walk replaces it"). D7 places the deploy-and-external-walk after a failure-free round, as optional.

requirement: The repository holds only what a session must read or a merge must carry.
note: Its check is REC-10, a candidate.

requirement: A tranche can run from open to close with no one watching: every stop is a named blocker in the record, ARCH starts other work meanwhile, and only a blocker that only the owner can clear reaches him (the owner's own words).
note: D2 restates "can run" as "runs".

requirement: Each job in its own checkout; its cost per attempt is an alarm the sweep reads, not a cap.
kind: MECHANISM (purpose: lack of progress is caught)
note: The own checkout stands. Evidence against the cost alarm, as JOB-10: cost figures were frequently unobtainable (product_side, limits; change_sample PRs 105, 106). An alarm (section 5).

requirement: A rule, check, review round, measurement run or owed task exists only against a measured failure or the owner's word; a finding with neither is one line in a report and changes nothing.
note: As F-HUM-13.

requirement: Status names each role's next acts from git alone, so a fresh architecture session given only status takes the right next act.
note: Leans with D9 (no handoff scanning).

requirement: No role waits on ROOT or a scheduled task for work the record allows: a job's report or a merge wakes ARCH at once, and a scheduled wake only catches a session that stopped.
note: D4 needs it. Measured 2 Nov: 194 minutes late with no event.

requirement: The owner's standing approvals in each repository's CLAUDE.md are the one policy for every act at every depth; the start check confirms each session loaded the tip's; the deny list holds only hard prohibitions.
kind: PURPOSE (one policy, in his hand); MECHANISM (the start check)
note: Conflict APPR: the approvals reach sessions only as a file the owner commits by his own hand, which D1 excludes ("does not enter commands or edit source files"); the platform facts that force that channel are measured (quoted consent declined 11 of 11; the judge refuses a session writing them). D9 lists permission refusals first. Evidence on the start check is at F-MNT-1.

requirement: A public release or promotion to installed sites waits for the owner's approval through the protected GitHub environment; development releases are drafts and need none.
note: Conflict REL: approving a release is an owner act that is not a settings change (D1) and a wait on him (D2). D7 speaks only of the optional deploy-and-external-walk.

requirement: On one plain request the process stops development under one Claude account and writes a tested page of steps to restart under another.
note: Conflict TOP: the page's steps are the owner's and are on the Claude side (the cloud environment, Claude's GitHub connection), not GitHub or Cloudflare settings (D1). The need was real: the merging identity changed on 7 Nov with a 9.3-hour silence (product_side §7, §9). The evidence is against the size of the mechanism only (causal_forensics §4.2).

requirement: The Ledger, the Foundations and the Build Plan agree: each section and row cites the Ledger lines it serves, and no build starts on a line any of them contradicts.
note: The purpose stands; D11 and this table serve it. Evidence against citation as the mechanism: a session restored a check the owner had removed, citing Ledger lines (change_sample PR 185). D1 to D11 now override conflicting lines, so "contradicts" has to be read against them.

requirement: Review findings go to the job as diagnosis; review is never the merge gate; a green gate merges without the owner, who approves a particular merge only when he asks to.
note: Fits D2. Whether review itself remains is the conflict at INT-2.

requirement: A platform behaviour is measured once by default, more only when the first result is ambiguous or a failure recurs.
note: Leans with D9. Section 5.

requirement: The tranche report states ARCH's idle time while work was ready and the minutes of the owner's it took.
kind: MECHANISM (purpose: urgency and his time are measurable)
note: The only stated measures of D1 and D2. A measurement (section 5).

requirement: Nothing here is in force until it has run on a real tranche with the two health metrics measured.
note: Whether the two metrics still judge is at F-SHAPE-5. Section 5.

requirement: A build plan is derived from the document and reviewed, assessed and evolved; implementation starts only when the result will work for projects large and small, for Civicsmith and the products after it.
Every account, setting and branch rule is listed, checked before each job starts, and set by the developer through the fewest steps, each with its reason and tested to work the first time.
note: The purpose stands and fits D1. Evidence against "checked before each job starts" is at F-SET-3; the owner cut it to once per pin on 9 Nov (DECISIONS.md PD-21).

requirement: The setup list names each condition: what it is, why, its value and who sets it; it is reviewed like code.
note: Reviewed like code follows INT-2 (section 5).

requirement: The setup check reads every condition at onboarding and before every job start; a missing one stops the start; it only reads.
kind: MECHANISM (purpose: no job meets a missing setting as a refusal)
note: Evidence: it refused every job start on the copy after the owner applied new settings; read a Cloudflare 429 as "missing" and stopped a pin move; grew to about 15 minutes, twice per pin move; lived 7.0 days and was cut to once per pin on the owner's word on 9 Nov (change_sample PR 15; removal 296).

requirement: One document, the developer's steps, lists only the acts the developer must take, each with why; each product gets one onboarding page; ARCH does every other part of onboarding.
note: Conflict TOP: the listed acts include the cloud environment, which is set on the Claude side and is not a GitHub or Cloudflare setting (D1). The secrets, Actions settings and collaborators it lists are GitHub settings.

requirement: Sessions act on GitHub as a collaborator that can push and merge but cannot change settings; the owner acts as the owner.
note: Fits D1: settings are his.

requirement: GitHub holds: every branch refuses deletion and force-push; main and the tranche take changes only by pull request, merge commits only, with the gate and record required. The deny list holds the rest, including the plain merge routes.
note: These are the rule settings D1 leaves to the owner. The required "record" check follows REC-10 (section 5).

requirement: A session reads the deny list only when it holds one repository and starts from a branch that carries it; every session starts from the tranche.
note: A platform fact (section 6).

requirement: The process deploys so walkers can run, so a project runs unattended only if it can deploy.
note: Changed by D6 (the round's walk is internal) and D7 (the deploy-and-external-walk is optional and follows a tranche): unattended running no longer rests on deploying. The definition must say what deploying is needed for.

requirement: Deploy tokens are added to the cloud environment as environment variables; the setup check confirms each by name.
note: Evidence: the token check read a Cloudflare 429 as "missing" and stopped a pin move (change_sample removal 235). Audit C also cites a Cloudflare token and signing seeds sitting beside product code in the session environment (redteam_feasibility, finding 11; not re-read here). D1: the cloud environment is a Claude-side setting. Platform fact the other way: environment variables were the one route both the deploy tools and the setup check were measured to read (2 Nov).

requirement: Deploying, releasing and acting on a live site are ARCH's acts, not a job's.

The checks hold against mistakes and outsiders' fork pull requests; a deliberate attack is held by GitHub's walls and the owner's approval for production; a finding that needs a deliberate attack is a known limit, not code.
note: D9 leans the same way. Five of seven kept trust rules guarded something never observed (change_sample §5).

requirement: Every session starts at the tranche's tip by commit and first verifies the pin, HEAD and the approvals block; on a mismatch it acts on nothing; a change to approvals is taken up by replacing long-lived sessions.
note: The candidate is the fail-closed approvals part. Evidence, with its limit: the owner's own commit was read as a forbidden settings change 15 times (change_sample §5, PR 234); his last approvals edit merged at 16:45Z on 9 Nov and no product landing followed, but "Git cannot show why that edit stopped the sessions" (product_side §8). Starting by commit rests on a platform fact (section 6).

requirement: Re-test at each model release and each Claude Code version change; the approval test reruns too.
note: Reported refusal rates moved several-fold between versions (Foundations). A trial of the process (section 5).

requirement: Per tranche: commits by purpose, sessions per job, gate runs per merged job, restarts, tokens by role; the tranche report states elapsed time, work done, deferrals, cost, the overhead share, ARCH's idle time and the owner's minutes.
kind: MECHANISM (purpose: the process is honest about its cost)
note: As SES-11, PLN-6 and GAP-12. Measurements (section 5).

requirement: False-done rate: the share of COMPLETE claims refuted by the gate's re-run and revert check, from the first tranche.
note: It earned its place: 20 false "complete" claims refuted by the suite in one day (change_sample §5). It counts on the gate's re-run and the revert check, both in conflict CHK. A measurement (section 5).

requirement: Cost per surviving pull request: tokens or dollars per pull request still in place after a two-week revert window.
note: Survival is readable from git (98.8%, product_side §5). Evidence against the cost half: sessions "frequently could not obtain a cost figure" (product_side, limits; change_sample PRs 105, 106). The definition must say how cost is held or named unmeasured (SES-9).

requirement: Usage is read by an allowed route or named unmeasured.
The process is judged by two numbers; they are the standing judge of every other line.
note: As F-SHAPE-5.

requirement: The process owns what can be proven in git and CI and nothing on a live site; rollout and operations are the owner's, through the protected environment.
note: His approval there is the conflict at GAP-7.

requirement: Release packaging is the Release workflow (installer artifact, update manifest, signing, draft releases); a development release stops as a draft; install-from-scratch and upgrade tests run as release-tier fixtures first.
kind: MECHANISM (purpose: a release can be cut without him until publication)
note: Packaging stands. The release-tier install and upgrade tests are tests outside D6's three ("no others, ever"); the definition must say what becomes of them (section 5). The owner's 8 and 9 Nov decisions on these workflows are DECISIONS.md BD-R1, BD-R3 and BD-R5.

requirement: Coming back: the walk's findings after a deployment enter the next round as entries.
note: Fits D6(iii) and D7.

requirement: A development release is cut and deployed by the process in each round, without the owner, to the product's own site, reaching no one else, on his standing approval.
note: Without the owner stands. The cadence is replaced by D7 ("A round that completes without any failures ends a tranche, after which an optional multi-session deploy-and-external-walk runs") and D6 (the round's walk is internal). His words of 8 Nov already said so (DECISIONS.md PD-16). Evidence: all 12 development deployments failed and none ran for 80 hours (product_side, summary 3).

requirement: A public release is a development release the walkers have passed, published only with the owner's approval; the production environment holds the publishing job and the keys, never the sessions' cloud environment.
note: Conflict REL (as GAP-7).

requirement: Dropped: the hook refusing partial reads (ENF-4).
note: Platform fact: hooks vanished after a resume. Its named replacement, the citation audit, is REC-8, a candidate.

requirement: Dropped: the Stop hook enforcing the refresh threshold (ENF-5).
Dropped: the mandated test-first red step (INT-6).
note: Its named replacement includes the revert check (JOB-12, conflict CHK).

requirement: Dropped: the twelve-module process architecture (MNT-2).
Dropped: in force the day written, certified on a toy (MNT-12).
Dropped: the repository doorbell and mailboxes (MSG-7).
Dropped: the git-synced multi-writer tracker (REC-12).
note: Its named replacement, the JSON ledger, is REC-9, a candidate.

requirement: Dropped: every rule names the principle it serves (P16).
note: Its named replacement, citation of a failure, is TXT-6, a candidate.

requirement: Decide stateless against long-lived architecture session by tokens per wake (SES-16).
note: Never measured; as SES-16. Section 5.

requirement: Decide the JSON ledger on whether sessions corrupt or bypass it (REC-9).
note: As REC-9; the measure set here appears in no post-mortem file.

requirement: Measure the architecture session's routing share of its context (SES-15).
note: Not measured. Section 5.

requirement: Decide which lanes run as long-lived sessions and which as workers (SES-14).
note: Not measured. Section 5.

requirement: Set the requirements cap number from reading-set sizes and job outcomes by module size (REQ-6).
note: As REQ-6.

requirement: Decide the home for transient state on repository growth, writer conflicts and status latency (REC-1).
note: As REC-1: the number is in (12,881 state-branch commits, 70% of all).

requirement: Permission mode per role: settled 1 Nov, every role runs in Auto; denials per role are counted in the metrics (SES-8).
note: The count measures D9's first interruption. Section 5.

requirement: Merging without a person: settled at 0 refusals in about 450 acts in the confirming round.
note: A settled measurement (section 6).

requirement: Mutation sampling on payment and data paths, decided by mutation score after the first tranche (JOB-13).
note: D6: "exactly three tests and no others, ever".

requirement: Decide the model and effort table by tokens per merged pull request (SES-8).
note: Not measured; token figures share JOB-10's evidence. Section 5.

requirement: ROOT stays a session and, with the sweep and the watcher, creates and refreshes the architecture session; the owner starts ROOT, and replaces it only if the watcher declines.
note: Conflict TOP: starting or replacing ROOT is an owner act that is not a GitHub or Cloudflare setting (D1); the platform creates sessions only from a person, ROOT or a task, and a task's fresh session could not start sessions (0 of 3). Cost of the mechanism on record: 1,738 heartbeat, idle-check and session-list commits (product_side §3).

requirement: A layer closes when every pull request is merged and the layer's checks pass; whole-product checks run before a release.
note: D5: "The layer construct is dropped". D6: "No regression or deploy-and-walk between layers" and "The full regression is ended". As INT-4.

requirement: The settings file carries only hooks ENF-1 allows; the drift check fails on any other; today there are none.
note: The drift check follows SHM-1 (section 5).

requirement: ARCH routes between spokes and does not translate every exchange; it explains toward the owner with context, in words he understands.
note: As SES-15.
